neighbours.label: The slot just before a technical property term is named in science prose ('an effect known as', 'a property called', 'is highly'), predicting a term like hysteresis, plasticity or non-linearity; quiet on the same science descriptions without a naming slot.
fire: Some metals return to their original shape when heated, a phenomenon known as shape memory.
The ability of nerve cells to strengthen their connections is a property called synaptic plasticity.
Light bends as it passes from air into water, an effect known as refraction.
Under heavy load the polymer slowly deforms, a behaviour called creep.
Glass breaks suddenly without bending, a property known as brittleness.
The loss of resistance in some metals at very low temperatures is called superconductivity.
The output of the amplifier rises unevenly, a behaviour known as non-linearity.
Some liquids get thinner when stirred, a property called shear thinning.
quiet: Some metals return to their original shape when heated, and engineers use them in springs.
Nerve cells strengthen their connections when they are used together often.
Light bends as it passes from air into water, which makes a straw look broken.
Under heavy load the polymer slowly deforms over several weeks.
Glass breaks suddenly without bending when it is dropped on stone.
Some metals lose all resistance at very low temperatures in the laboratory.
The output of the amplifier rises unevenly when the input gets louder.
Some liquids get thinner when stirred for a few minutes.

predictions: median fire ~0.5 (probes: 'a property called' 0.88, 'known as h' 0.81, 'is highly' 0.41, 'strongly' 0.25); near misses < 0.2 (recorded at high voltages 0.04, bread 0.006). 'is very old' reached 0.16.
notes: Card: 'known as h|ysteresis', 'called ‘neuroplasticity’', 'highly non-linear', 'highly plastic'. Causal: reads the naming slot, so near misses remove the naming construction.
